findings.issue: Paragraph 5.4 and the support-body row present the full new-office estimate for a council the bill sets up without any secretariat, office or positions. Applying the estimate to a body that creates no office misleads the reviewer, and these become the only peso figures in Part V for a bill whose real costs are fleet replacement and charging facilities.

Paragraph 5.1 and the continuing-funding row recommend absorbing vehicle replacement within regular vehicle budgets, while the same row warns that higher upfront costs may exceed those budgets; the recommendation is not reconciled with the risk it states.

Not raised: LGUs and GOCCs are told to fund acquisition, charging, maintenance and training from their own budget proposals, so the transition cost falls on entities outside the GAA. Part V does not analyse this unfunded mandate or which lower-capacity LGUs would be left out.
findings.quote: Covered government entities shall incorporate the necessary expenditures for vehicle acquisition, charging infrastructure, maintenance, and personnel training into their respective annual budget proposals

findings.issue: Part V treats the transition only as added cost. It does not ask covered entities to show fuel and maintenance savings, or proceeds from disposing of replaced vehicles, as offsets in their budget proposals, which the Part IV mid-term evaluation already treats as relevant.

Paragraph 5.1 proposes charging the initial requirement against available appropriations in the year of effectivity, but the bill already places it in the DOE and implementing agencies' GAA appropriations; Part V does not say why that route is preferred or how it fits the pilot phase.
findings.quote: The initial amount necessary to carry out the provisions of this Act shall be included in the appropriations of the DOE and other concerned implementing agencies

findings.issue: Paragraph 6.1 adds the signing date of RA No. 12231, which the rules flag as signature content and the analysis does not need.
The BMB-A reason (DPWH and DOTr share responsibility for charging infrastructure) is not supported by the bill material provided; the reason should be checked against the bill.

No bureau handling GOCC budgets and no Legal Service referral are listed, although GOCCs are covered entities and Part IV raises GFI lending to government entities and a local-assembly procurement preference that need legal review.
